name: Wular Lake
ecologicalImportance: Largest natural freshwater lake in India; acts as a natural flood reservoir for the Jhelum River basin in Kashmir Valley.
examFacts: Formed by tectonic activity and fed by the Jhelum River, which enters at Sopore and exits at Baramulla.
Designated as a Ramsar Wetland of International Importance in March 1990.
Contains the artificial island of Zaina Lank built by 15th-century Kashmir Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin.
Supports massive commercial fisheries and water chestnut (Singhara / Trapa natans) extraction for local livelihood.

name: Chilika Lake
ecologicalImportance: Largest brackish water lagoon in Asia and the second largest coastal lagoon in the world; premier wintering ground for migratory waterfowl in the Indian subcontinent.
examFacts: India's first designated Ramsar Wetland site (1 October 1981).
Successfully restored and removed from the Ramsar Montreux Record in 2002 after opening a new tidal sea mouth at Sipakuda.
Nalabana Island inside the lake is declared a bird sanctuary, hosting over a million migratory birds during peak winter.
Primary habitat for the endangered Irrawaddy Dolphin (Orcaella brevirostris) in India.
Separated from the Bay of Bengal by a 60-km long barrier beach and sandspit.

name: Loktak Lake
ecologicalImportance: Largest natural freshwater lake in Northeast India; famous for floating islands called Phumdis and the endemic dancing deer (Sangai).
examFacts: Keibul Lamjao National Park on its southern rim is the world's only floating national park.
Home to the endangered Eld's deer subspecies Sangai (Rucervus eldii eldii), which lives exclusively on the phumdis.
Placed on the Ramsar Montreux Record in 1993 due to ecological degradation caused by the construction of the Ithai Barrage.
Phumdis are thick, floating mats of soil, decaying vegetation, and organic debris used by fisherfolk for temporary settlements called Khangpok.

name: Vembanad Lake (Vembanad-Kol)
ecologicalImportance: Longest lake in India (~96 km) and the largest lake in Kerala; core of the famous Kerala backwaters ecosystem.
examFacts: Designated as a Ramsar Wetland of International Importance in November 2002.
Thanneermukkom Bund (saltwater barrier) divides the lake into two parts: freshwater southern section and brackish northern section.
Hosts the celebrated annual Nehru Trophy Boat Race (Vallam Kali) on the Punnamada lake stretch on the second Saturday of August.
Kuttanad below-sea-level farming system (recognized as FAO GIAHS) lies along its southern periphery.
Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary is located on the eastern shore of the lake.

name: Sambhar Salt Lake
ecologicalImportance: India's largest inland saline lake; critical wintering ground for tens of thousands of migratory flamingos (Phoenicopterus roseus and minor).
examFacts: Produces approximately 9% of India's total salt via brine evaporation pans.
Designated as a Ramsar Wetland in March 1990.
Receives drainage from five seasonal rivers: Mendha, Runpangarh, Kharian, Khandel, and Samod.
Endorheic depression surrounded on all sides by the ancient Aravalli Range.

name: Lonar Crater Lake
ecologicalImportance: Hyper-saline soda lake formed by a high-velocity hyper-velocity meteorite impact in basalt rock during the Pleistocene epoch (~50,000 years ago).
examFacts: One of only four known hyper-velocity impact craters in basaltic rock anywhere on Earth.
Water is simultaneously hyper-saline (pH ~10.5) and alkaline, harboring rare haloarchaea and halo-alkaliphilic microbes.
Designated as a Ramsar Wetland of International Importance in November 2020.
Surrounded by ancient temples including the 12th-century Daitya Sudan Temple built during the Yadava dynasty.
